why: Quote and cited line both check out, but the CONSEQUENCE is false — the classic 'identifier is unwired, something upstream already handled it' shape. (1) QUOTE: verbatim at best-practices.md:532, second sentence of a two-sentence line ('Refine your prompt based on what goes wrong with the first 2-3 files, then run on the full set. The `--allowedTools` flag restricts what Claude can do, which matters when you're running unattended.'); the first sentence does not reverse it. (2) CITED LINE: apps/cli/src/index.ts:842 reads exactly as claimed, and `grep -an 'allowedTools|allowed-tools'` over apps/cli/src returns 0 hits — no such flag; the 24 parsed flags are --url --token --workspace --timeout --json --tls-ca --send-timeout --source --mode --output-format --json-schema --no-cleanup --disable-spinner/--no-spinner --verbose --safe-mode --server-entry --workspace-dir --provider --model --api-key --base-url --help --version --validate-server. bypassPermissions is indeed the widest mode (PERMISSION_MODE_ORDER, mode-types.ts:63). (3) CONSEQUENCE — REFUTED. An enforced tool allowlist with exactly the semantics the sentence describes DOES exist and it outranks bypass. `checkToolPermission` (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts) evaluates, IN THIS ORDER: deniedPaths :2094, deniedToolPatterns :2103, disallowedTools :2111, `config.allowedTools` :2119-2127 ('Tool blocked: <tool> is not included in allowedTools') and deny/ask toolRules :2129-2157 — and ONLY THEN, at :2161, does `if (mode === 'bypassPermissions') return { allowed: true }`. A non-empty allowedTools list therefore blocks every tool off it even in bypassPermissions. Those lists come from permissions.json layers that the merged config assembles (permissions-config.ts:8 'Workspace: CONFIG_DIR/workspaces/{slug}/permissions.json' and per-source; loadWorkspacePermissionsConfig :698 applied :1107, allowedTools pushed :1252), so scoping IS reachable per invocation: `--workspace <slug>` selects the workspace whose permissions.json carries the list, and `--source` scopes the enabled capability/MCP tool set per run. pre-tool-use.ts adds two more floors bypass does not skip — `requiresUserInteraction` (:1161-1169, 'even in ... bypassPermissions') and the rm -rf / circuit breaker (:1186-1200, 'unlike EVERY other gate in this file it is NOT skipped'). So 'no per-invocation tool scoping' and 'running unrestricted' are both wrong; what is actually missing is only the one-flag ergonomic. (4) PAGE SCOPE: best-practices is row 115 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md, verdict ⬜ in the section 'Вне продукта — платформы, IDE, облака, онбординг' — a tips page grouped with common-workflows and champion-kit. The normative page for a CLI flag is cli-reference (row 37, 🟨), not this one. Not one of the nine §3 owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md, and the bypass default is long-standing documented CLI behaviour (docs-site/content/reference/cli.md:185 '| `--mode <mode>` | `bypassPermissions` | permission mode for the session |'; line 842 only respelled `allow-all` → `bypassPermissions` in 5e8c5b76).
correctedState: apps/cli has no `--allowedTools` flag (0 hits, `grep -a`), and `nessy-general-agent run` defaults to `bypassPermissions` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:842) — both as claimed, and the default is documented at docs-site/content/reference/cli.md:185. But the consequence does not follow. An `allowedTools` allowlist with the same restricting semantics is implemented and enforced at packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts:2119-2127, ahead of the `bypassPermissions` short-circuit at :2161, alongside deniedPaths (:2094), deniedToolPatterns (:2103), disallowedTools (:2111) and deny/ask toolRules (:2129) — so a bypass run is not unrestricted. The lists live in the permissions.json layers (workspace CONFIG_DIR/workspaces/{slug}/permissions.json, per-source, global, managed), which the CLI selects per invocation with `--workspace` (and `--source` for the capability/MCP tool set, `--safe-mode` to strip skills/plugins/hooks/MCP, `--mode` to start from a prompting mode). The real, much smaller gap is ergonomic: there is no single per-run flag that sets the allowlist inline the way `claude -p --allowedTools "Edit,Bash(git commit *)"` does, so a fan-out script must pre-stage a workspace permissions.json instead.
